To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Chevalley-Weil theorem holds for etale covers of curves over number fields, and that this can be used to find number fields with large (or small) class groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: given an integer n > 1, does there exist a finite set of primes such that, for all sufficiently large primes p not in the set, the class number of the ring of integers of the unique quadratic extension of Qp is divisible by p?

the following problem: given a finite group G, find all number fields whose class group has order divisible by |G|, or, more generally, find the number of number fields whose class groups have a subgroup isomorphic to G.
the following questions: (i) What are the possible specializations of a given étale cover of curves over the complex numbers?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can find number fields of any given degree with arbitrarily large class groups, and that we can count them in terms of a finite sum.
the number of number fields with class number greater than $n$ is at least $\frac{1}{2}n^{2}+o(n^{2})$.

, for a fixed number of primes, the probability for a randomly chosen extension of number fields of degree n with class group of order d to have at least one prime of degree n/d is asymptotically bounded away from 0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to construct, for any given integer k, a number field K with class number k, and a subgroup of the class group of K of index k, which is isomorphic to a subgroup of the ideal class group of the Hilbert class field of K.
we can construct a number field K with class group of size at least n for any positive integer n.
we are able to construct and count number fields whose class group contains a subgroup isomorphic to a given finite abelian group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the class groups of number fields are not as random as one might think.
the Chevalley-Weil theorem is not just a tool for constructing number fields with a large class group, but also a tool for constructing large subgroups of class group of a given number field.
the number of subgroups of the class group of a number field can be bounded below by a function of its discriminant.
